core_sentence: Domain-specific sampling, if required, may also be specified in the relevant DSAs.
dsa_evidence: no additional clinical testing is specified in this protocol

core_sentence: At initiation of a new domain, the proportion of participants allocated to each intervention is balanced (i.e., all interventions have equal proportions), unless otherwise specified in a DSA.
note: No statement on initial allocation. DSA 6 is not a domain initiation.

core_sentence: Unless otherwise specified in a DSA, when a new intervention is added to an existing domain it will commence with balanced randomization (equal to 1/K where K is the number of interventions in the domain) and the randomization proportions will be updated with each subsequent adaptive analysis.
note: No statement on allocation for an added intervention.

core_sentence: For domains without a control arm, no formal minimum or maximums are set unless specified in the DSA.
dsa_evidence: The decision regarding the reference control can only be made after having achieved a trigger for efficacy
note: Domain has a 'no corticosteroid' comparator now. After its removal (pre-specified in 10.1) the domain has no control arm, and the Core default would then apply. Is 'no corticosteroid' a control arm in the Core sense?
open_question: Is 'no corticosteroid' a control arm in the Core 7.5.2 sense, and does the no-control-arm default apply after its removal?

core_sentence: For domains with only two available interventions, the default is that RAR will not be applied, unless specified in the DSA.
dsa_evidence: Response Adaptive Randomization may be applied.
note: Three interventions overall, but hydrocortisone is Severe State only (8.3.1), so the Moderate State has two. Does 'may be applied' override the two-intervention default for the Moderate State?
open_question: Does CS_DSA 10.3 'RAR may be applied' override the Core two-intervention default (no RAR) for the Moderate State, where two interventions are available?

core_sentence: The primary outcome for this Platform will apply to all domains, unless otherwise specified in a DSA.
dsa_evidence: The primary endpoint for this domain is the primary outcome as specified in Core Protocol documents.
note: Unversioned; resolves differently under Core 4.0 and 4.1 (see CQ1, Core 4.1 7.6.2).

core_sentence: If required, details related to blinding of interventions will be specified in the DSAs.
dsa_evidence: All corticosteroids will be administered on an open-label basis.

core_sentence: Any alternative gamma that will be set, and hence the unit-of-analysis, for each domain-Strata pair will be specified in each DSA.
dsa_evidence: The statistical model will permit borrowing between all strata as specified in Core Protocol documents.
note: No alternative gamma; Core borrowing taken. 10.2 also fills the unit-of-analysis strata.

core_sentence: The lambda that will be set for each domain-domain pair is specified in each DSA.
dsa_evidence: Interactions with all other domains are either not evaluable or not considered possible and will not be incorporated into the statistical model

core_sentence: Whether nested analysis will be performed and, if so, the membership of category of more similar interventions will be specified in the DSA.
dsa_evidence: Nesting is not applicable to this domain.

core_sentence: If informative priors are used this will be specified in the relevant DSA.
note: No statement on priors. Silence read as 'none used'; the Core sentence is conditional ('If informative priors are used').

core_sentence: Early phase interventions or seamless Phase 2/Phase 3 domains may have a separate set of triggers not specified in the Core Protocol, which will be specified in the relevant DSAs.
note: Not an early phase or seamless Phase 2/3 domain (no statement either way). 10.8 sets an equivalence delta, which is not this delegation.

core_sentence: For RAR, allocation proportions will be capped at 60% for two-intervention domains, unless otherwise specified in a DSA.
dsa_evidence: the cap on the maximum or minimum proportion of patients assigned to an intervention that is specified in core protocol documents may be modified by the Statistical Analysis Committee (SAC)
note: Takes the Core cap, but delegates further: SAC may modify it, as an operational decision in the Current State document. Applies to two-intervention domains: same Moderate State question as row 78.
open_question: Does the Core 60% cap for two-intervention domains apply to the Moderate State, where two interventions are available?

core_sentence: Individual processes for specific domains will be specified in the relevant DSA documents.
note: Generic delegation of 'individual processes'; no single answering statement. Proposal: keep out of CQ2.

core_sentence: Whether interventions are open-label or blinded will be specified in DSAs.
dsa_evidence: Patients will be randomly assigned to receive one of the following open-label study interventions.

core_sentence: The criteria for discontinuation specific to each domain are specified in the relevant DSA.
dsa_evidence: Refer to relevant core protocol documents for criteria for the discontinuation of participation in this trial.
note: Circular: Core 8.6 says domain-specific criteria are in the DSA; the DSA points back to the Core. Note: DSA speaks of discontinuation of participation in the trial, Core of discontinuation of an allocated intervention.

core_sentence: Prespecified co-interventions related to specific domains will be recorded in the CRF and are outlined in the relevant DSAs.
dsa_evidence: All use of systemic corticosteroids is recorded and the reason for any new or additional administration will be documented.
note: 8.4 also: etomidate after enrollment not permitted.

core_sentence: Additional domain-specific variables are outlined in the relevant DSAs.
dsa_evidence: Additional domain-specific data will be collected.

core_sentence: Whether or not an intervention is regarded as having an established safety profile, and any additional reporting requirements, will be specified in the relevant DSA.
dsa_evidence: Other SAEs should be reported only where, in the opinion of the site investigator, the event might reasonably have occurred as a consequence of a study intervention or study participation
note: Reporting requirement is stated; 'established safety profile' is not stated explicitly (11.3 says corticosteroids have been used for decades).
open_question: Does CS_DSA 11.2 answer the 'established safety profile' part of Core 8.12.1, or only the reporting part?

core_sentence: The trial endpoints, as outlined in the Core Protocol and as specified in DSAs, are designed to capture the majority of events that might otherwise constitute an SAE.
dsa_evidence: serious adverse events (SAE) as defined in the Core Protocol
note: Core sentence is descriptive rather than a delegation; Step 2 classification 'delegates' to be reviewed.
open_question: Is Core 8.12.3 'as specified in DSAs' a delegation or a descriptive statement? (Step 2 classification kept.)

core_sentence: If required, additional clarification of issues related to the identification of SAEs that are relevant to a specific domain will be described in the DSA.
dsa_evidence: Potential domain-specific harms related to corticosteroid therapy include hyperglycemia, nosocomial infections and ICU-acquired weakness.
